mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to increased borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-tightening periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days, reflecting stronger labor market confidence.
failure_condition: In 20-day walk-forward, returns are not statistically positive when the trigger is met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1100 for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating resilient consumer demand supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of 5 points or more predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns, reflecting supply-side weakness and reduced corporate earnings momentum.
failure_condition: During regime with INDPRO decline, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced labor market friction and improved investor sentiment.
failure_condition: Over 12 months, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during pre-trigger periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 2023 Q4 averages for the next month predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, capturing dual demand signals.
failure_condition: In 20-day window, forward return not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite trigger met.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 3% for two consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return, reflecting reduced cost pressures and improved equity valuation sensitivity.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When a combination of GDPC1 (GDP) decline and PAYEMS (employment) contraction of 10,000 or more jobs occurs in a month, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative, signaling supply-side weakness.
failure_condition: In 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative when trigger is met (p > 0.05).
